submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires retrospectively at sparse landmark tokens inside text that reproduces a standardised, verbatim-recurring formula — an open-source licence/copyright header block in comment form ('Copyright (c) <year> <holder> … All rights reserved', Apache/BSD/GPL lines at their usual line layout), a 'Code generated by … DO NOT EDIT' banner, a standard tool dump (docker info, SQL-dump header), or rows of a templated dataset such as 'What is the greatest common factor of X and Y?' (one prior row is needed and it saturates by the third). It is near baseline on authored prose, chat, hand-written code and ordinary comments, bibliographic or tabular records (citations, ISBN, invoices, CSV, YAML, HTTP headers), self-repeating text and famous quotations, so the trigger is a standard formula that recurs verbatim across documents rather than repetition or memorability as such; its negative pole instead fires on narrative calendar ' year' phrases (see L17/N3233−).

One way to find it is to list the factors of each number and look for the biggest one they share: the factors of 24 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 24, and the factors of 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18 and 36, so the greatest common factor of 24 and 36 is 12. For larger numbers the listing method gets slow, so most people use Euclid's algorithm instead: divide the larger number by the smaller one, then keep dividing the previous divisor by the remainder until the remainder is zero, and the last non-zero remainder is the answer.

explanation_scores.explanation: Fires retrospectively at sparse landmark tokens inside text that reproduces a standardised, verbatim-recurring formula — an open-source licence/copyright header block in comment form ('Copyright (c) <year> <holder> … All rights reserved', Apache/BSD/GPL lines at their usual line layout), a 'Code generated by … DO NOT EDIT' banner, a standard tool dump (docker info, SQL-dump header), or rows of a templated dataset such as 'What is the greatest common factor of X and Y?' (one prior row is needed and it saturates by the third). It is near baseline on authored prose, chat, hand-written code and ordinary comments, bibliographic or tabular records (citations, ISBN, invoices, CSV, YAML, HTTP headers), self-repeating text and famous quotations, so the trigger is a standard formula that recurs verbatim across documents rather than repetition or memorability as such; its negative pole instead fires on narrative calendar ' year' phrases (see L17/N3233−).
